title: Efficacy of combination therapy with isavuconazole and intermittent high doses liposomal amphotericin B for the treatment of mucormycosis
official: CombiMucor - Efficacy of combination therapy with isavuconazole and intermittent high doses liposomal amphotericin B for the treatment of mucormycosis
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the efficacy, based on the favorable global response at week 4 (W4), of a combination therapy involving ISZ and a short, intermittent, high-dose L-AmB regimen for initial treatment of mucormycosis

interventions.name: CRESEMBA 200 mg powder for concentrate for solution for infusion
AMBISOME liposomal 50 mg, poudre pour dispersion pour perfusion

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Adult ≥18 years
2. Probable or proven localized mucormycosis, according to modified EORTC/MSGERC criteria (including diabetes and trauma as host factors, and incorporating one positive serum qPCR as a diagnostic criteria for probable mucormycosis), ), enrolled no later than five days after initiation of curative treatment for mucormycosis
3. Female subjects of childbearing potential has agreed to use highly effective birth control for the duration of treatment (4 weeks) and until 32 days after the last dose of study medication
4. Subject (or close relative) has provided written informed consent
5. Beneficiary of a social security coverage (affiliated or entitled)
Exclusion criteria:
1. Patient with disseminated mucormycosis
2. Concomitant treatment with no possibility of stopping before inclusion with strong CYP3A4 inducers such as rifampin, carbamazepine, St. John's Wort, or long-acting barbiturates or with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors such as ketoconazole or high-dose ritonavir (>200 mg every 12 hours)
3. Patients receiving palliative care or whose life expectancy is expected to be less than a month, excluding mucormycosis
4. Patient with a positive ßHCG test, pregnancy or breast-feeding
5. Participation to another clinical interventional trial on medicinal products for human use
6. Cerebral mucormycosis, defined by a radiological lesion in the nervous central system suggestive of mucormycosis
7. Patient hospitalized in the Intensive Care Unit at the time of inclusion AND who has active hematological malignancy or solid organ transplantation,
8. Previous curative L-AmB or ISZ treatment > 5 consecutive days within the previous 15 days before inclusion
9. Concomitant coinfection with cryptococcosis
10. Severe allergy to polyene or azoles
11. Known hypersensitivity to peanut or soy
12. Severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class C)
13. Patient with known familial short QT syndrome
